title: Margaritaville Resort Biloxi (Wikipedia)
quote: The casino opened on June 5, at a cost of $55 million.
summary: Casino Magic Corp announced the Biloxi barge in January 1993 and it opened on June 5 of that year (1993, not 1992). The 1992 date belongs to the company's Bay St. Louis casino.
limits: Wikipedia; year inferred from the January 1993 announcement in the same article. Not an official record.

title: Margaritaville Resort Biloxi (Wikipedia)
quote: In October 1998, the property came under the ownership of Hollywood Park, Inc. (later Pinnacle Entertainment), which bought Casino Magic Corp. for $340 million.
summary: Casino Magic Corp (to 1998), then Hollywood Park/Pinnacle; Pinnacle later traded the property to Harrah's.
limits: Wikipedia.

title: Margaritaville Resort Biloxi (Wikipedia)
quote: giving Casino Magic plus $25 million to Harrah's Entertainment
summary: After Katrina destroyed the casino barge in 2005, Pinnacle exited Biloxi by handing Casino Magic plus $25 million to Harrah's. Hotel later reopened as non-gaming Margaritaville Resort Biloxi (June 23, 2016). The casino did not reopen.
limits: Wikipedia. Exact year of the Harrah's transfer (2006) not stated in the passage.

title: Controversy over ex-regulators landing casino jobs
quote: Instead of continuing to police the casino operators, he joined them, doubling his salary and becoming a senior vice president for Casino Magic
summary: 1998 news report on the regulator-to-industry revolving door: the first Mississippi Gaming Commission director became a Casino Magic executive. It is a regulatory-ethics story and alleges no organised-crime tie.
limits: Journalism, 1998; says nothing about mob involvement.

title: Pete Halat (Wikipedia)
quote: The FBI investigation eventually ended the city's long tolerance for wide open, illegal gambling and striptease clubs with exorbitantly priced drinks
summary: Biloxi's Dixie Mafia convictions (1997 racketeering conspiracy conviction of the former mayor) concerned the 1987 Sherry murders and the city's illegal vice scene, not the licensed 1990s casinos.
limits: Wikipedia. Does not tie any licensed casino to the Dixie Mafia. Subject is a living person; no accusation is made here beyond his recorded conviction, cited for context only.

title: President Casino Broadwater Resort (Wikipedia)
quote: Entrepreneur John E. Connelly, founder of President Casinos, then gained control of the property, and the President Casino Broadwater Resort was opened aboard a riverboat
summary: Opened August 1992 aboard a riverboat at the Broadwater marina; destroyed with the resort site by Hurricane Katrina on August 29, 2005 after Broadwater Development LLC bought it in April 2005. Confirms 1992 to 2005.
limits: Wikipedia.

title: President Casino Broadwater Resort (Wikipedia)
quote: Broadwater Development LLC – a casino holding company owned by two local construction figures
summary: Thread: Broadwater Beach Hotel (1939, Pete Martin Sr.), Joe Brown 1958, Dorothy Brown, President Casinos (John E. Connelly) 1992, bankruptcy 2002, Broadwater Development LLC 2005; barge sold to Silver Slipper venture.
limits: Wikipedia.

title: President Casino Broadwater Resort (Wikipedia)
quote: He openly ran a casino within the hotel, as even though it was nominally illegal at the time
summary: The site's 1939 illegal gambling under a rum-runner owner predates the 1992 casino; the article describes a bankruptcy-driven business history for the casino era and no organised-crime finding.
limits: Wikipedia; pre-1992 gambling is not a crime-syndicate finding.

title: Boomtown New Orleans (Wikipedia)
quote: opened its Boomtown Westbank casino on August 6, 1994.
summary: Boomtown Inc opened Boomtown Westbank on August 6, 1994; infobox names it Boomtown Westbank 1994-2002, now Boomtown New Orleans. Still open.
limits: Wikipedia.

title: Boomtown New Orleans (Wikipedia)
quote: The property became part of Hollywood Park, Inc. (later Pinnacle Entertainment) with its purchase in 1997 of Boomtown, Inc.
summary: Boomtown Inc (1994) to Hollywood Park/Pinnacle (1997); property sold to Gaming and Leisure Properties and leased back to Pinnacle in 2016; now operated by Penn Entertainment.
limits: Wikipedia; infobox gives Penn Entertainment as licence holder. Penn's 2018 acquisition of Pinnacle is not in the page text I read.

title: Boyd Gaming (Wikipedia)
quote: Boyd owned 15% of the property at its 1994 opening, before acquiring Treasure Chest outright in 1997
summary: Treasure Chest (Kenner) opened 1994 with Boyd holding 15%; Boyd took full ownership in 1997.
limits: Wikipedia (Boyd Gaming article); the Treasure Chest article itself is only a redirect there. Local investors' names not given.

title: Edwin Edwards (Wikipedia)
quote: He also appointed a board that, at his private direction, awarded 15 floating riverboat casinos
summary: Context: Louisiana's 1990s riverboat licences were awarded under Governor Edwards, who was later convicted of racketeering and extortion over riverboat licensing (public corruption). This page does not name Treasure Chest or tie any of these venues to organised crime.
limits: Wikipedia; the underlying 5th Cir. opinion (United States v. Edwards, 303 F.3d 606) could not be opened (justia and ca5 blocked), so no documented label is claimed. Subject died in 2021.

title: IP Casino Resort Spa (Wikipedia)
quote: The property opened for business officially on December 22, 1997, as the Imperial Palace Hotel and Casino Biloxi.
summary: Opened Dec 22 1997 as Imperial Palace Biloxi, sister of the Las Vegas Imperial Palace; founded by Ralph Engelstad.
limits: Wikipedia, flagged 'one source' on the page.

title: IP Casino Resort Spa (Wikipedia)
quote: Boyd Gaming bought the IP in October 2011 for $278 million in cash
summary: Engelstad (1997); his estate/trustees after 2002; Boyd Gaming from October 2011.
limits: Wikipedia. Closure or later ownership after Boyd not covered.

title: Ralph Engelstad (Wikipedia)
quote: the Nevada Gaming Commission fined Engelstad $1.5 million
summary: The only regulator action on the founder in these sources is the 1989 Nevada fine over Hitler-birthday parties at his Las Vegas casino, a reputational matter, not organised crime.
limits: Wikipedia; concerns the Las Vegas property, and says nothing about Biloxi.

title: Beau Rivage (Mississippi) (Wikipedia)
quote: The Beau Rivage, with 1,740 rooms, opened in March 1999.
summary: Opened March 1999; heavily damaged by Katrina Aug 29, 2005 and fully reopened Aug 29, 2006. Name was originally intended for Bellagio; developer Steve Wynn's Mirage Resorts.
limits: Wikipedia.

title: Beau Rivage (Mississippi) (Wikipedia)
quote: Ownership of the Beau Rivage, along with many other MGM properties, was transferred to MGM Growth Properties in 2016
summary: Mirage Resorts (Wynn) developer; MGM Mirage parent by 2009; MGM Growth Properties owner 2016, MGM Resorts operator (page now also says Vici Properties owns it).
limits: Wikipedia. Mirage-to-MGM merger year not stated in the page; no mob material appears in it.

title: Caesars New Orleans (Wikipedia)
quote: Originally opening in 1999 as Harrah's New Orleans, the casino holds the status of being the only land-based casino in the state of Louisiana.
summary: Permanent casino opened in late October 1999 (closed after Katrina, reopened Feb 17 2006); predecessor Harrah's Jazz ran a temporary casino from 1995, filed for bankruptcy in November 1995.
limits: Wikipedia.

title: Caesars New Orleans (Wikipedia)
quote: In 2020, it was announced that the casino would be rebranded as Caesars New Orleans, with the name officially changing in May 2024.
summary: Harrah's Jazz (Hemmeter/Caesars World/Harrah's, 1993-95), Harrah's New Orleans 1999-2024, Eldorado acquired Caesars Entertainment 2020, Vici Properties bought the real estate for $790 million, renamed Caesars New Orleans May 2024.
limits: Wikipedia.

title: Caesars New Orleans (Wikipedia)
quote: was resolved when the two entities formed a joint venture under pressure from then-Governor Edwin Edwards.
summary: The 1993 licence/lease impasse was resolved by a political push from the governor; the page reports business and political dealings and no organised-crime link.
limits: Wikipedia.

title: Hard Rock Hotel & Casino Biloxi (Wikipedia)
quote: The resort opened on July 7, 2007.
summary: Planned opening September 2005 was cancelled when Katrina destroyed the barge; soft opening June 30 2007 and grand opening July 7 2007 on a land-based site. The record's 2007 matches (the property never opened in 2005).
limits: Wikipedia. Its predecessor on the site was the Gold Shore Casino.

title: Hard Rock Hotel & Casino Biloxi (Wikipedia)
quote: In July 2014, Twin River Worldwide Holdings acquired the property from Leucadia National for $250 million.
summary: Premier Entertainment Biloxi LLC (Leucadia) 2002 with Hard Rock licence; Twin River 2014; Bally's name for the company, but the resort keeps the Hard Rock name (2021); real estate sold to Gaming and Leisure Properties and leased back January 4 2023.
limits: Wikipedia.

title: Golden Nugget Biloxi (Wikipedia)
quote: In 2012, the casino was sold to Fertitta Entertainment to be converted to a Golden Nugget.
summary: Property began as Isle of Capri Biloxi; sold to Fertitta Entertainment in 2012 and rebranded Golden Nugget Biloxi.
limits: Wikipedia.

title: Isle of Capri Casinos (Wikipedia)
quote: Isle of Capri Casinos opened its first casino in Biloxi, Mississippi in August 1992
summary: The Biloxi casino now called Golden Nugget opened as Isle of Capri in August 1992 (the first on the Gulf Coast), so the record's 2012 opening year is a rebrand date, not an opening date.
limits: Wikipedia; 'citation needed' tag on the NASDAQ clause; the Biloxi site's casino barge was destroyed in 2005 and later rebuilt (not detailed in the text I read).

title: Golden Nugget Biloxi (Wikipedia)
quote: In 2005, the casino, but not the hotel, was destroyed by Hurricane Katrina.
summary: The 1992 Isle of Capri casino was destroyed by Katrina in 2005 (hotel survived); the site later reopened (reopening date not stated on this page).
limits: Wikipedia.
